events.title: Austria-Hungary Declares War on Serbia
events.description: One month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, Austria-Hungary declared war on the Kingdom of Serbia, formally beginning hostilities that would draw in Europe's major powers.
events.significance: Marked the official start of World War I, a conflict that reshaped global borders, toppled empires, and caused millions of deaths.

events.title: Fourteenth Amendment Certified
events.description: U.S. Secretary of State William Seward certified that the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution had been ratified by the required number of states.
events.significance: Guaranteed citizenship and equal protection under the law to all persons born or naturalized in the United States, including formerly enslaved people, and became a foundation for later civil rights litigation.

events.title: B-25 Bomber Crashes into the Empire State Building
events.description: A U.S. Army Air Forces B-25 Mitchell bomber, lost in heavy fog, struck the north side of the Empire State Building in New York City between the 78th and 80th floors.
events.significance: The crash killed 14 people and led to improvements in aviation safety and air traffic procedures; the building was repaired and reopened quickly.

events.title: Execution of Maximilien Robespierre
events.description: Robespierre, leader of the Committee of Public Safety, and a number of his allies were guillotined in Paris following the Thermidorian Reaction that overthrew him a day earlier.
events.significance: Ended the radical phase of the French Revolution known as the Reign of Terror and shifted France toward the more moderate Thermidorian regime and eventually the Directory.

events.title: Birth of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
events.description: Jacqueline Lee Bouvier was born in Southampton, New York; she later became First Lady of the United States as the wife of John F. Kennedy.
events.significance: Known for her style, her restoration of the White House, and her promotion of the arts and historic preservation, she became a lasting American cultural icon.
